title: Top K Frequent Elements
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return a list of the k distinct values that appear most often in nums. Order the result by frequency from highest to lowest; when two values occur the same number of times, the smaller value comes first. k is guaranteed to be at least 1 and at most the number of distinct values in nums, so a valid answer of length exactly k always exists.
hints: You need to know how often each value occurs before you can rank anything. What structure gives you counts in one pass?
Build a hash map from value to occurrence count, then select the top k distinct keys. The required order is descending count with ties broken by ascending value.
Sort the map's keys with a compound key like (-count[v], v) so higher counts come first and equal counts fall back to smaller values first, then slice the first k keys.
